bull_bear.body: Confident, disciplined, and strategic — prioritizing margin resilience over aggressive growth, emphasizing operational excellence, backward integration, and API-plus innovation; tone is calm, data-driven, and focused on long-term sustainability

bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- ROICE is tracking at ~32% in Q1FY27 (34% FY23, 32% FY24, 27% FY25, 30% FY26), which the deck attributes to a "calibrated Capex strategy".
- Free cash flow of ₹901 Mn in the quarter took cash and cash equivalents (including short-term investments) to ₹8,802 Mn as of 30 June 2026, described as a strong balance sheet.
- Finance costs are negligible at ₹13 Mn in the quarter, consistent with the net-cash posture; the deck states ongoing investments in capacity expansion and pipeline development are "strengthening the foundation for future growth".
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Portfolio of 176 high-value, non-commoditised APIs concentrated in chronic, high-burden therapies - the AR frames these as niche and technically complex rather than commodity molecules
- Regulatory track record: three plants regularly inspected and approved by the USFDA and other key regulators, described as over two decades of stringent compliance
- Breadth of regulatory filings - 611 DMF/CEP filings across the US, Europe, Japan, Russia, Brazil, South Korea, Taiwan, Canada, China and Australia - which is a barrier to switching for formulator customers
- Customer franchise: 900+ customers across 75+ countries with business relationships with the top 20 generic pharmaceutical companies worldwide
- Complex-chemistry capability at scale - Grignard, hydrogenation, bromination and oxidation - supported by in-house solvent recovery units
- Three advanced R&D centres plus a fourth under construction at Taloja; sustained R&D spend and a pipeline of specialised, differentiated and technically complex molecules
- Parentage of Nirma Limited, which the MD's message credits with enhanced financial strength, long-term stability and greater flexibility to invest
- Net debt-free balance sheet with all planned capital expenditure funded entirely through internal accruals
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Regulatory / facility inspection risk — An adverse facility inspection by any regulator may cause restriction in sales to certain customers or respective geographies. Structural for a business whose sales into the US, Europe, Japan and other regulated markets depend on maintaining plant approvals; the Company mitigates through systems to continuously monitor compliance and employee training on compliance updates.
- Supply chain - single-source supplier dependency — The failure of a small number of single-source, third-party suppliers or service providers to fulfil their contractual obligations in a timely manner, or through regulatory non-compliance or physical disruption at their manufacturing sites, may result in delays or service interruptions that materially and adversely affect revenues. Mitigated by developing alternative sources, an inventory strategy where dual sourcing is not possible, and backward integration projects for critical items.
- Market risk - price, competition, geopolitics and foreign exchange — Losses can arise from price fluctuations, the competitive scenario, geopolitical events, foreign exchange fluctuations, worldwide pandemics and other events affecting market movements. Mitigation cited: cost reduction and efficiency measures, resource reallocation to identified growth opportunities, launching differentiated value-added products that can fetch better pricing, and a Board-approved hedging policy for currency exposure.
- Employee recruitment, development and retention — BRSR material issue. The ability to attract, develop and retain skilled talent is a key challenge given the specialised and highly regulated nature of the API industry and the limited availability of qualified professionals with technical and compliance expertise; gaps in recruitment or retention can impact operational efficiency, product quality and business performance. Mitigated through targeted recruitment, structured training, internal mobility and an AI-based continuous listening mechanism for engagement.
- Counterfeit or substandard drugs / product integrity — BRSR material issue. For an API manufacturer, any compromise in product authenticity or quality can lead to serious regulatory consequences, reputational damage and loss of customer trust, with increasing regulatory scrutiny and traceability requirements. Mitigated by batch-level testing for identity and purity, traceability mechanisms across the supply chain and continuously strengthened quality assurance systems.
- Water, wastewater and hazardous waste management — BRSR material issues. API manufacturing is water-intensive and inherently generates hazardous waste; high consumption, improper effluent handling or improper waste disposal can lead to regulatory penalties, operational disruptions, remediation costs and reputational impact. Mitigated via ETPs with primary, secondary and tertiary treatment, reuse of treated water, STPs for domestic wastewater, condensate and RO-reject reuse, replacement of steam ejectors and water-based vacuum systems with dry alternatives, and disposal of landfillable waste through authorised CHWTSDF facilities.
- GHG emissions and energy intensity — BRSR material issue. API manufacturing is energy-intensive and dependence on conventional energy sources raises emissions and the carbon footprint, against increasing regulatory focus on climate change. Mitigation includes optimising HVAC, compressors, pumps and blowers, automated controls and fan cut-off sensors, replacement of outdated equipment with energy-efficient transformers, chillers and vacuum systems, condensate recovery and steam-system efficiency, and a stated target of becoming Carbon Neutral by 2030.
- Employee health and safety — BRSR material issue. API manufacturing involves handling chemicals and operating complex equipment, so lapses in safety practice can cause injuries, operational disruptions and regulatory consequences. Mitigated through a safety culture supported by leadership commitment, regular risk assessments, appropriate PPE and ongoing training for employees and contract workers.

business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Regulated markets contributed 83% of Q1FY27 revenues, with the deck noting the market mix has remained largely stable (83%/81%/83%/85%/83% across Q1FY26-Q1FY27) "despite of ongoing geopolitical uncertainties".
- Regulatory estate is the stated moat: 617 cumulative DMFs and CEPs filed as of 30 June 2026 across the United States, Europe, Japan, Russia, Brazil, South Korea, Taiwan, Canada, China and Australia.
- Revenue is split Generic API 94% and CDMO 6%, so the company is presented as an API-first business with CDMO as an emerging second leg.
- Reducing dependence on the former parent is the central structural theme: non-GPL business is now 88.7% of revenue (from 74.6% in Q1FY26), with GPL down to 11.3%.
- Manufacturing sites carry multi-jurisdiction approvals (USFDA, MHRA, EDQM, FIMEA, PMDA, COFEPRIS, Health Canada, KFDA, ANVISA, state FDAs), with the most recent USFDA inspections at Ankleshwar in Jan 2025 and Dahej in May 2025.

business.body:
- [Rename] The company is Alivus Life Sciences Limited, formerly Glenmark Life Sciences Limited (CIN L74900PN2011PLC139963; NSE ALIVUS, BSE 543322).
- [Customer concentration] GPL (Glenmark Pharmaceuticals Ltd.) revenue de-grew 52.6% YoY on inventory rationalization to ₹723 Mn / 11.3% of revenue; management expects recovery in H2FY27 and a flattish full year, noting GPL business "has historically been skewed towards H2".
- [Guidance] Management guides to FY27 revenue growth of 10%-12% while "sustaining EBITDA margins in the 30%-32% range" — below the 36.6% EBITDA margin reported for Q1FY27 and the 33.6% for FY26.

business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Alivus develops and manufactures a portfolio of 176 high-value, non-commoditised APIs primarily for chronic and high-burden therapy areas such as cardiovascular, CNS, diabetes, oncology, urology and pain management, and is broadening beyond APIs through an 'API+' strategy that adds differentiated products, advanced manufacturing technologies, stronger R&D and a scaling CDMO business. Its customers are end formulators - pharmaceutical manufacturers that convert its APIs into finished products - and it states relationships with the top 20 generic pharmaceutical companies worldwide across regulated and emerging markets. It also collaborates with innovator companies on post-generic lifecycle management offerings.

outlook.body: Solapur Phase 1 (370KL BI + 120KL API) to enable backward integration and regulated market supply; Taloja R&D center for flow chemistry, pellets, granules; 28 high-potency API molecules in pipeline (12 validated, 7 advanced); API-plus expansion into complex molecules; Japan market scaling
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- 'API+' - deliberately expand capabilities beyond traditional APIs by adding flow chemistry, complex molecules, high-potent APIs, pellets and granules, end-to-end product development and a stronger CDMO platform, so the Company participates across a wider portion of the pharmaceutical value chain.
- Continue the product and geographic diversification strategy begun when the Company became a standalone API business seven years ago - management says it is now driving both growth and margin improvement, and will continue to drive the pipeline.
- Grow the CDMO business, which recovered during the year as existing projects gained traction and newer projects scaled up.
- Prioritise quality of growth over growth itself: growth will not be pursued at the cost of quality, product differentiation or profitability.
- Capital allocation - retain and reinvest cash rather than distribute it, maintain a net debt-free balance sheet, and fund all planned capital expenditure entirely through internal accruals.
- Deploy capital into the Solapur greenfield manufacturing project, the new Taloja R&D centre and technology platforms for the next phase of growth.
- Continue to evaluate inorganic opportunities that complement existing strengths and create meaningful synergies - disciplined expansion, not diversification for its own sake.
- Operational strategy of expanding capacity while becoming more energy efficient - bio-briquette based boilers for steam (stated to have made cost of operations extremely stable given global gas-supply uncertainty), reduced water, electricity and steam usage, and automation initiatives for material handling.
- Environmental target of becoming Carbon Neutral by 2030, stated as the Company's approach to mitigating and neutralising carbon emissions and thereby significantly reducing the impact of GHG emissions.
- Water circularity programme: ETPs with primary, secondary and tertiary treatment, reuse of treated water where feasible, STPs for domestic wastewater, recovery and reuse of condensate streams, reuse of RO reject and HVAC condensate as boiler feed, and process modifications replacing steam ejectors and water-based vacuum systems with dry alternatives to eliminate water-intensive operations.
- Hazardous waste governance: waste suitable for landfilling is transferred to authorised Common Hazardous Waste Treatment, Storage and Disposal Facilities (CHWTSDF), with internal processes for segregation, handling and tracking.
- Energy-efficiency programme cited as directly lowering fuel consumption and emissions: optimisation of HVAC systems, compressors, pumps and blowers, automated controls and fan cut-off sensors, and replacement of outdated equipment with energy-efficient transformers, chillers and vacuum systems.
- Governance of risk: a Risk Management Committee of the Directors has been constituted under SEBI LODR, comprising Mr. Kaushikbhai Patel (Chairman), Dr. Yasir Rawjee and Mr. T. L. Easwar; it met twice in FY26.
- Zero complaints reported under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition & Redressal) Act, 2013 during F.Y. 2026, with an Internal Complaints Committee in place covering all women employees including temporary, contractual and trainees.
- Customer grievance handling: a Standard Operating Procedure under which all complaints are formally acknowledged within two working days and outcomes communicated within thirty working days, supported by a dedicated Customer Experience team and regional single points of contact.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Alivus operates four multi-purpose, cGMP-compliant API manufacturing facilities - Ankleshwar and Dahej in Gujarat, and Mohol and Kurkumbh in Maharashtra - with installed reactor capacity stated at 1,424 KL in FY26. A fifth site, a greenfield API facility in the Chincholi Industrial Area, Solapur, was under construction during the year (BRSR excludes it from the plant count for that reason) and is being developed to manufacture both APIs and intermediates in several multi-purpose blocks with mid-to-high volume capacity, serving both the generic API and CDMO businesses; Phase 1 is expected to add 465 KL of reactor capacity, with subsequent phases extending into backward integration of Key Starting Materials (KSMs). At Ankleshwar, the Company commissioned its first continuous manufacturing process in FY26 with one global product commercialised using flow chemistry, and construction of three additional pharma blocks is underway which is expected to be operational by Q4 FY27, adding approximately 100 KL of reactor capacity. At Dahej, two independent manufacturing modules have been commissioned and are operational, with additional capacity of 160 KL planned for FY27. Capacity additions at Ankleshwar, Dahej and Solapur are described as on track for commissioning through FY27, supported by upgraded warehousing, effluent treatment and utility infrastructure designed for higher throughput, and are intended to support projected commercial-scale manufacturing volumes of over 900 MT in FY27 (against 888 MT produced in FY26). On the R&D side, a new R&D centre is underway at Taloja (Navi Mumbai) with capabilities for the API and CDMO businesses, adding to three existing R&D centres. Management states 'we have invested in Capex of INR 473 crores, and paid dividend of INR 61 crores. This leaves us with a war chest of INR 423 crores', and that all planned capital expenditure continues to be funded entirely through internal accruals on a net debt-free balance sheet, with the Company also positioned to grow inorganically through investments in API+. Development-stage platforms behind the build-out include a High Potent API (HPAPI) portfolio with 28 products in the active development grid (12 validated, seven in advanced stages, nine in laboratory development) addressing an estimated TAM of USD 73 billion, and an iron complexes portfolio with one product filed, one in advanced development, one in laboratory development and one under feasibility evaluation, targeting a TAM of USD 2.7 billion.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Customers increasingly seek partners offering scientific depth, regulatory excellence, resilient supply chains and support across a broader spectrum of requirements - success is no longer determined by manufacturing excellence or cost competitiveness alone.
- Global outsourcing is shifting towards partners that offer integrated development capabilities under a single roof and can support customers with more than just the API/product in the value chain; customers are consolidating relationships with such partners.
- India is being recognised not merely as the 'Pharmacy of the World' but as a strategic partner for innovation, process development and resilient supply chains, as global companies diversify sourcing and reduce concentration risks.
- Mix and margin levers cited for FY26: favourable product mix, execution on several new launches across geographies, disciplined cost management, new operational efficiencies and an increasing focus on high-value differentiated products.
- The non-GPL business grew 13% during the year, increasing its contribution to 71% of overall revenues, while revenue from operations grew 6.9%.
- Highest-ever EBITDA margin of 33.6% in FY26 was delivered despite the absence of PLI benefits, which were withdrawn after FY24.
- External environment flagged as a drag: geopolitical uncertainty, evolving trade dynamics and supply chain disruptions - management says its strategy remains unchanged in response.
- Energy-cost stability from bio-briquette based boilers, cited as insulating the cost of operations from global gas-supply uncertainty and sharp gas-price increases.
- No order book is disclosed. Management states it can 'see this playing out with huge interest in our oncology pipeline from across geographies' - a qualitative pipeline demand signal rather than a quantified order book.

deepdive.thesis: Alivus delivered record 33.6% EBITDA margin in FY26 despite losing PLI benefits, driven by a sharp shift to higher-margin non-GPL (71% of revenue) and CDMO recovery, with Solapur Phase 1 set to commission in Q2FY27 and a robust 611 DMF/CEP pipeline positioning it for sustained margin resilience and growth beyond FY28.

open.item: Solapur delayed ~3 months; now expected to start operations by July 2026, with initial ROW business and validation; regulated products from Solapur by late FY28.
Solapur Phase 1 (370 KL backward-integration block + 120 KL API block) to be operational in Q2 FY27, starting at ~40-50% utilization rising to 60-70% next year.
Ankleshwar and Dahej brownfield expansions to become operational in Q2 FY27, giving ~2-year reg-market runway.
Hope to close 2 new CDMO deals in early second half of FY27 (may slip slightly from H1).
Ankleshwar/Dahej brownfield capacity to reach 80-90% utilization within 2-3 quarters (approved sites).
Non-GPL business (71% of FY26 revenue) growing at double digits (13% in FY26) expected to continue; GPL to shrink as share.
Construction of three additional pharma blocks at Ankleshwar is underway and expected to be operational by Q4 FY27, adding approximately 100 KL of reactor capacity.
Additional capacity of 160 KL is planned for the Dahej site in FY27, following two independent manufacturing modules already commissioned and operational there.

open.horizon: Phase 1; capacity additions at Ankleshwar, Dahej and Solapur stated as on track for commissioning through FY27
open.item: Phase 1 of the greenfield API facility in the Chincholi Industrial Area, Solapur is expected to add 465 KL of reactor capacity, with subsequent phases extending into backward integration of Key Starting Materials.
Capacity additions are expected to support projected commercial-scale manufacturing volumes of over 900 MT in FY27, against 888 MT produced in FY26.

Capacity additions at Ankleshwar, Dahej and Solapur are on track for commissioning through FY27, supported by upgraded warehousing, effluent treatment and utility infrastructure designed to handle higher throughput.

War-driven freight and solvent cost inflation (solvents ~12-13% of cost) largely being passed on to customers who have agreed to reasonable price rises; operations cost stable (switched gas to briquette boilers).
Backward integration on key projects to begin once Solapur is online in H2 FY27, expected to lift margins.
New R&D center in Taloja, Navi Mumbai under construction.
FY27 capex of ~INR540 crores (carryover + fresh), funded entirely through internal accruals.
Confident of sustaining EBITDA margins in the 30% to 32% range going forward (FY27); full-year margin guidance to be firmed up as war impact clarifies.
CDMO projects 4 and 5 together expected to top out ~$12m (possibly higher) around H2 FY27; three legacy projects run ~INR140 cr.
Guiding to high single-digit revenue growth for FY27 as well, with margins in 30-32%; implies ~15-17% volume growth net of ~5% erosion.
9M FY26 growth net of ~5% price erosion is volume; FY27 base case assumes ~5% erosion and ~15-17% volume growth.
Solapur greenfield expansion (incl. 400 KL backward integration) underway; part of FY25-FY28 capex plan.

verdicts.item: Beyond FY25, comfortable returning to early double-digit growth in generics and faster CDMO growth (moving 3 to 5 CDMO projects next year).
verdicts.note: Generics (non-GPL) returned to double-digit growth: 'in the non-GPL business, we are already growing at double digit' with FY26 non-GPL +13%.

verdicts.item: FY26 capex of ~INR550-600 crores (INR190 cr carryover + INR350-400 cr new), Board pre-approved.
verdicts.note: Actual FY26 capex came in far below the INR550-600 crore plan: 'capex for the year being INR306 crores.'

verdicts.item: Asset turns to be lower near-term during investment phase, gradually reaching ~2x over time.
verdicts.note: Asset turns lower during the investment phase as flagged, heading toward ~2: 'it would go down a little bit more... it would temporarily go down below 2 as well... it would come back up once the utili…

verdicts.item: Typical price erosion ~4-4.5% on the pipeline going forward, more on newer high-volume products.
verdicts.note: Price erosion assumption confirmed: 'on the overall bucket, we do see an erosion of around 4.5%'; base business (ex-GPL, ex-CDMO) erosion ~5.5%.

verdicts.item: US customer destocking on CDMO side caused soft FY25 CDMO; expected to remain back-loaded in FY26.
verdicts.note: The back-loaded FY26 CDMO recovery played out: 'We also witnessed a meaningful recovery in the CDMO business from Q3 of FY26, as existing projects gained traction and newer projects scaled up.'

verdicts.item: Potential US pharma tariffs a watch-item; industry bodies pushing back; API likely treated differently from finished dose; outlook seen positive with possible small upside.
verdicts.note: Tariffs remained a watch-item/headwind but were managed: 'we have faced some headwinds like uncertainties around tariffs and regulatory shifts... Alivus has not only navigated this environment success…

verdicts.item: 4th CDMO project to reach full potential by end of FY26; 5th project (Japanese innovator) regulatory approval now expected in H2 FY26 (slipped from H1).
verdicts.note: Fifth project commercialized ('fourth and fifth project have kicked in really nicely') but full potential of projects 4+5 tops out only in H2 FY27, not end-FY26.

verdicts.item: New R&D center near Mumbai to be built at a cost of ~INR70-80 crores.
verdicts.note: R&D center materializing: 'construction of the new R&D center in Taloja in Navi Mumbai is also underway'; cost not restated and not yet complete.

verdicts.item: Brownfield pharma expansions at Ankleshwar and Dahej to come online by early H2 FY26 (Nov-Dec 2025).
verdicts.note: Ankleshwar/Dahej brownfields past Nov-Dec 2025: they become operational in Q2 FY27, reaching '80%, 90% level in a matter of 2 to 3 quarters.'

verdicts.item: Solapur Phase I (300 KL) expected to come online in Q4 FY26.
verdicts.note: Solapur Phase I pushed from Q4 FY26: 'Solapur Phase 1... expected to be operational in Q2 of this year.'

verdicts.item: EBITDA margins to remain in the 28% to 30% band for the foreseeable future.
verdicts.note: Margins beat the 28-30% band: 'We delivered EBITDA margins of 33.6%, expanding by 360 basis points.'

verdicts.item: Maintains FY26 guidance of mid-teens volume growth.
verdicts.note: Non-GPL volume was mid-to-high teens (13% growth net of ~5.5% erosion) but total FY26 growth of +6.9% was held back by flat GPL, so overall volume fell short of mid-teens. [±10% rule]

wtt.summary: 62% guidance hit (20 chains); 5/18 projects on-time; 1 expired; 15% theme consistency (info)
wtt.tone_latest: Very confident after record FY26 margins; management owned the Dahej fire (INR20 cr) and modestly pushed the 2 new CDMO deals to early H2, while firmly defending a high-quality-over-aggressive-growth philosophy.
